views.reconstructed_statement: For every c,s ∈ ℝ, let R(c,s) be the complex 2 by 2 matrix [[c,-s],[s,c]], where real entries are canonically embedded in ℂ. Then R(c,s) is unitary if and only if c²+s²=1 in ℝ. Using the supplied interfaces, unitarity means R(c,s)†R(c,s)=I₂, where † denotes conjugate transpose and I₂ has diagonal entries 1 and off-diagonal entries 0.

views.reconstructed_statement: For every coefficient : Type u, selector : Type v, and system : Type w, each equipped with Fintype and DecidableEq, and every complex square matrix P=prepare indexed by selector, if P is unitary then L=I_coefficient ⊗ (P ⊗ I_system) is unitary on coefficient × (selector × system). The product and tensor factors have exactly this order and right association. For row (a,(b,t)) and column (a′,(b′,t′)), the entry is δ_{a,a′} · (P(b,b′) · δ_{t,t′}), where each δ is complex 1 on equality and 0 otherwise. Equivalently the entry is P(b,b′) if a=a′ and t=t′, and 0 otherwise. The theorem is the one-way implication P†P=I_selector ⇒ L†L=I_{coefficient×(selector×system)}.
